headline: A 2013 House resolution would have continued veterans' benefit funding at current levels through December 15, 2013, but the House voted it down.
what_it_does: It would have provided temporary funding for veterans' benefits that are paid automatically under existing law, keeping them at the same rate as the prior year's rules. The funding would have run until December 15, 2013, or until a full FY2014 appropriations law took over. It would also have allowed mandatory payments due in the months after October 2013 to continue. The resolution further suggested it could be called the Honoring Our Promise to America's Veterans Act.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans receiving mandatory federal benefit payments
who_it_affects.how: Their monthly and other scheduled benefit payments would have continued during a funding gap instead of being interrupted.

who_it_affects.group: Staff of the Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Benefits Administration
who_it_affects.how: Their operations would have been funded at a set rate under the prior year's terms until the continuing period ended.
